card.summary: No quota at all. Relay operators cap themselves with -global-rate (commonly ~20 Mbps in and out). The pool is anonymous and unvetted.

free_tier.stated: No quota at all. Relay operators cap themselves with -global-rate (commonly ~20 Mbps in and out). The pool is anonymous and unvetted.

egress.terms: Free. Paid for by whoever runs each relay, not by a company with a budget.

record.interface_detail: relay:// protocol on 22067; the pool is a JSON endpoint.
record.chaining: Relay is only used until a direct connection is established; Syncthing then switches to direct and the relay carries nothing.
record.limits_note: Per-relay bandwidth set by the operator; sessions per client and per relay are limited. Relays can vanish without notice.
record.reliability_note: The pool endpoint returns dozens of `relay://IP:22067` entries with self-signed device IDs. No accounting means no sustainability, but also no gate.

evidence.proved: literal JSON list of relay:// URLs with IDs
'Anyone can run a relay server, and it will automatically join the relay pool'
traffic is bounced via a relay only when a direct connection is impossible
'The relays listed on this page are not managed or vetted by the Syncthing project'

record.notes: No quota at all. Relay operators cap themselves with -global-rate (commonly ~20 Mbps in and out). The pool is anonymous and unvetted.
